races.name: Quooker Tap 100 Degrees Ebf Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Andersons - Quality For The Home Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Caturra Lights
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Adrian Keatley whose recent form reads 3-3-9 in good ground; 102-day absence is a flag to note, but the Carlisle 6f on soft suits horses who travel in behind and the jockey can slot in close enough to be dangerous.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive thirds two and three starts back mark Caturra Lights as a consistent threat, he carries 135 lb from stall two and has run over today's trip, and our rating has him clear on top; the main risk is a below-par return from 102 days off, highlighted by that ninth last time out.

runners_data.name: Fast Performer
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly-raced colt is only two runs in and has improved to second last time, handled by Cieren Fallon who will manage the pace intelligently; headgear worn and good-to-soft going both look fine, and his style is adaptable enough to press from just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Fast Performer has run over today's trip and steps back out after 34 days with a second two starts back giving him a solid recent profile; a trainer firing at 27% over the last 14 days boosts appeal, and our rating of 75 marks him as a leading contender despite being yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: North Star Kodi
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained hold-up type who has run identical thirds in his two starts, suggesting consistency but also a possible ceiling; Oisin Orr partners him and 105 days off is a concern — he needs to improve on recent evidence to land a nursery from this position.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last two starts, both thirds, North Star Kodi returns after 105 days off and has experience over today's trip, with our rating edging above his official mark offering a small foothold; the lengthy absence is the question he must answer.

runners_data.name: Social Spirit
runners_data.note: Easterby-trained youngster who has the most exposed form in the field, with six career starts and a telling 0W-0P record on similar going — sim-going figure of 1/6 suggests this surface is not enhancing his prospects, and his hold-up style is not well suited to a race with limited pace.
runners_data.comment: Social Spirit shaped with promise when third last time out and, fresh off a 20-day break carrying 130 lb from stall three, he has experience of today's trip and conditions to call upon; the concern is that he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Donegal Rose
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly won at Carlisle over this exact trip and is the race's sole pace-setter, giving her a structural advantage she has not had in all her starts; STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 arises because she is tagged as Prominent rather than Lead, but in this field she will effectively control from the front — discount that flag and rate the positional benefit highly.
runners_data.comment: Donegal Rose won three starts back but has since finished fifth and fourth before a tame ninth last time out, so her form is inconsistent at best; she has run over today's trip and carries 130 lb from stall 10, though 39 days off the track adds a further unknown.

runners_data.name: My Normandie
runners_data.note: George Scott's runner is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed into a midfield map position because the rear is overcrowded; 62 days off and a form line of 5-6-5-7 in good ground offers limited grounds for confidence, and racing closer than natural adds further complication.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and rated well below the field on our figures, My Normandie faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and carries 129 lb from stall five, but consistency has been elusive and 62 days off adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Gift
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's filly has the joint-lowest STYLE_FIT score (0.90) in the field — a true come-from-behind type who will find herself mapped into midfield rather than her natural deep-closing position; her only similar-going run was a seventh in soft and Tom Eaves will need things to fall perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Harlequin Gift faces a stiff task here, though a third last time out offers a crumb of comfort and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's colt is fascinating — a winner over 8f and placed over 6f, the drop back to this trip on a soft surface is intriguing, and while he is a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the redistribution, his form figure of 1-2-7-5-8 shows he is versatile enough to be competitive closer to the pace.
runners_data.comment: State of Gold arrives here on the back of a win last time out and a second two starts back, but that seventh three starts back tempers enthusiasm; she has run over today's trip and the 27-day break looks straightforward, though 129 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Ponte Carlo
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent type has been placed twice in seven starts and has a headgear note (p) suggesting he needs assistance to run his race; the sim-going record of 0W-1P in two runs on comparable going is modest, and though mapped into midfield his natural preference is to close from further back.
runners_data.comment: Ponte Carlo shaped with promise when third three starts back and stands on our rating of 74, suggesting he retains more ability than his official mark of 64 reflects; the concern is that he has gone winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Excessive
runners_data.note: The lowest-rated runner in the field and another Tim Easterby hold-up horse displaced into midfield by the field's composition; headgear worn (p), sim-going reads 0W-0P from one comparable run, and nothing in the form or trainer stats suggests he can overcome the structural disadvantage of racing against his natural style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Excessive is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after 29 days off a feasible weight of 121 lb from stall nine.

races.paceDynamic: Donegal Rose is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 6f nursery handicap on Good To Soft ground at Carlisle, and with no genuine rival to pressure her early, she is set to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, unhurried tempo. That controlled pace on a soft-ish surface over six furlongs will compress the field and limit the amount of daylight available to closers, making the race particularly kind to prominent and midfield types who can track the leader without burning energy chasing a breakaway. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours horses who can sit close to the pace in the early stages and pick off a front-runner who has had it too easy — prominent and stalking profiles hold a structural edge. The field contains significantly more hold-up and come-from-behind types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — State Of Gold, My Normandie, Harlequin Gift, Ponte Carlo, Excessive and Caturra Lights are all natural closers, and several will be forced into a more prominent position than they prefer, particularly State Of Gold and My Normandie who have the early speed to push closer if needed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Donegal Rose Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Donegal Rose breaks cleanly and settles into her natural front-running rhythm without anyone forcing the early pace.
scenarios.body: She bowls along on Good To Soft ground in a tactically uncontested lead, dictating tempo and ensuring only the fit and prominent-placed can live with her turning for home; horses who sit second or third from the off, close enough to strike, are best positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling second or third in the first half of the race produces enough to overhaul Donegal Rose in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The controlled tempo means those just off the pace never waste energy, arriving at the two-furlong marker full of running and able to pick off the front-runner as the soft ground bites; Caturra Lights or Fast Performer travelling smoothly in behind would be ideally suited.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffler Finishes Best
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses inside the final furlong and the softest ground drains the leaders, allowing a horse from mid-division to emerge.
scenarios.body: State Of Gold or My Normandie, forced closer than their natural style but still arriving with a late kick, could benefit if the front end folds earlier than expected; the redistribution of so many hold-up types into midfield means one of them racing slightly against type could still get competitive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Genuine Closer Defies Tactical Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than anticipated — perhaps multiple runners disputing the lead — and a true hold-up horse is gifted a strong gallop to close into.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the race to unravel in a way the pace map makes unlikely given only one front-runner is confirmed; Excessive or Ponte Carlo would need to produce career-best closing sectionals on ground they have mixed records on.

watchPoints.text: Donegal Rose's early break — if she jumps cleanly and gets a lead of two lengths by the first furlong, the race is very likely hers to lose; watch whether anyone pushes forward to challenge her, which would fundamentally change this race shape.

State Of Gold carries live each-way claims if jockey Clifford Lee positions him closer than his hold-up profile suggests is natural — his win over 8f and second over 6f show he can travel, and in a soft-ground race where front-runners are exposed, he could be dangerous.

The volume of hold-up horses forced into midfield (five runners tagged REDISTRIBUTED) creates a risk of bunching and interference through the first three furlongs — watch for crowding on the stands-side rail if the field splits or compresses.

Fast Performer (Cieren Fallon, Haggas) has only two runs and is the most lightly-raced horse in the field; with Fallon able to read pace supremely well and Haggas's horses rarely unfit on return, a big run at a potentially big price cannot be ruled out if he is dropped in just behind the leader.

Good To Soft going confirmed by the going report for this race — not Soft as the headline suggests — which slightly narrows the gap between ground-loving types and those who merely act on it; monitor any late ground movement before the off.

races.name: Lpd Maiden Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Lord Byron
runners_data.note: Front-runner allowed to bowl along on his own terms; four-year-old returning after 131 days for Faye Bramley, and soft going is not a major concern based on similar-going record; at 1m3f he sets the tactical shape for the whole field — the key question is whether his flat-race stamina holds across this trip.

runners_data.name: Togeather Forever
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with limited experience (two runs), both on soft/good-to-soft, so going is not an issue, but her form of 6-5 gives little confidence she can pick up from the rear if the pace is modest; Lauren Young claims 5lb which helps at the weights.

runners_data.name: Act Of Generosity
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old sits prominently and that style suits this controlled pace shape well; form reads 3-5 over 10f on good, stepping up to 1m3f on softer ground is the key query — if the trip is fine, the prominent position is the right one.

runners_data.name: Blue Hercules
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides a horse with genuine hold-up instincts who has been pushed into a midfield berth on the map because true rear-of-field positions are over-subscribed; his best form (placed three times at 12f on good) is solid, but racing closer than ideal on soft ground tests his adaptability.

runners_data.name: Casement Park
runners_data.note: Unraced three-year-old for Simon West, a handler who runs infrequently (0/1 in 14 days); no style, going, or form data available, so impossible to place in the pace shape — treat as a pure unknown with upside capped by lack of preparation signals.

runners_data.name: Chico Dorado
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore; Oisin Orr takes the ride which is a booking worth noting, but zero race data means the going suitability and tactical profile are entirely speculative — yard's 14-day strike rate of 0/9 does not encourage confidence.

runners_data.name: Flagbearer
runners_data.note: James Doyle partners this William Haggas hold-up type, whose trainer has a strong recent strike rate (13/48 in 14 days); soft-ground form is acceptable and the step to 1m3f looks a logical progression, but the modest pace set by Lord Byron is the significant tactical obstacle for a horse that prefers to be delivered late.

runners_data.name: Impierious
runners_data.note: Consistent but uninspiring — four consecutive thirds for Tom Clover, all at 8-10f on good ground; going is a concern on soft for the first time, but the prominent style is the right shape to adopt here and Cieren Fallon will likely have him close to the pace from the outset.

runners_data.name: Mighty Wave
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose true position is at the rear, not the midfield slot shown; his soft-ground form is reasonable (three runs, one placing) and the 1m3f trip is a positive step up, but Daragh Bourke's runner is compromised by the crowded closing section and a pace unlikely to generate the gaps he needs.

runners_data.name: Wadacre Icon
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's unraced three-year-old with Connor Beasley aboard; Johnston's 14-day strike rate of 2/32 is modest, but the stable regularly presents well-prepared debutants and the absence of form data makes this runner the most interesting wildcard among the three newcomers.

runners_data.name: Harper Violet
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's hold-up filly returns after 151 days — the layoff is notable — and she has placed on soft ground over shorter; Clifford Lee rides, and while soft Carlisle is not a concern, the extended absence and need for a strong pace at 1m3f to make her late run count are real negatives in this shape.

runners_data.name: Lazy In Red
runners_data.note: Donald Whillans's three-year-old has placed once in one soft-ground start over 11f, which is directly relevant form; Greg Fairley rides and the hold-up style is a tactical challenge in a race expected to be run at a restrained tempo — she needs things to happen late that this pace map suggests they won't.

races.paceDynamic: Lord Byron is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a 12-runner field on soft ground at 1m3f, he should be allowed to dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front. The pace will be modest rather than searching, which on soft Carlisle ground over this trip typically rewards horses who travel prominently and can quicken off a steady tempo rather than those relying on a late surge off a strong pace. Flagbearer, Harper Violet, and Lazy In Red are the true hold-up horses in the field, but with Blue Hercules and Mighty Wave both natural hold-up types redistributed into midfield slots — unable to get their preferred position at the rear because the map is congested — their late-run credentials are compromised. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to Lord Byron's moderate gallop and pounce turning for home, rather than closers who need a genuine pace injection that is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Lord Byron sets a controlled tempo and prominent types like Impierious and Act Of Generosity travel close to the pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Lord Byron dictates a manageable gallop on the soft ground, and horses who are close to the action from the outset avoid the energy cost of making up ground in testing conditions; the 1m3f trip at Carlisle rewards those who travel into the race rather than coming from off it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than anticipated and a genuine closer like Flagbearer or Harper Violet picks off a tiring field in the straight.
scenarios.body: A minor uptick in tempo — perhaps from Impierious pressing Lord Byron — could string the field out enough to open a gap for a late runner; Flagbearer with James Doyle's tactical nous and Harper Violet's soft-ground form could benefit if the pace does collapse into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debut Wildcard Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced runners — Casement Park, Chico Dorado, or Wadacre Icon — arrives with superior raw ability that overrides tactical uncertainty.
scenarios.body: Trainers of the calibre of Charlie Johnston and William Haggas-quality level are represented, and an unexposed maiden can bypass pace shape entirely when talent is decisive; Wadacre Icon (Johnston) and Chico Dorado are the debutants most worth monitoring.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Outnumbered Struggle
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the true hold-up horses — Blue Hercules and Mighty Wave — cannot access their natural position or generate meaningful momentum.
scenarios.body: Both horses are racing out of their preferred role having been pushed forward on the map by congestion, and a slow pace on soft ground at this trip is the worst-case environment for them; their chances depend on circumstances that are working directly against their profile.

watchPoints.text: Lord Byron controls the tempo entirely alone — if he is allowed to crawl through the early stages, midfield prominent types like Impierious and Act Of Generosity will have a significant advantage and closers including Flagbearer and Harper Violet will find the race over before they can wind up.

Blue Hercules and Mighty Wave are both genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield positions due to congestion at the rear — monitor whether they drift back to their natural ground in the early furlongs, as this would confirm the pace map's predicted shape and effectively eliminate their winning chances.

Three unraced debutants — Casement Park, Chico Dorado, and Wadacre Icon — create genuine unknown variables; if any arrives with superior ability the pace shape becomes secondary, and the Oisin Orr and Connor Beasley bookings on Chico Dorado and Wadacre Icon respectively are worth watching in the market moves.

The going is officially Good To Soft rather than Soft despite the Soft label in the race conditions — this is a meaningful distinction at Carlisle over 1m3f and could aid horses whose profiles show concerns at heavier ground, particularly Impierious who has only run on Good so far.

races.name: Deanta Fire Door Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Cape Sovereign
runners_data.note: 328 days off the track is a significant concern in a 13-runner sprint, and her hold-up style leaves her reliant on a clear run that cannot be guaranteed in this traffic; recent form on Tapeta offers little encouragement for today's turf conditions.
runners_data.comment: Cape Sovereign is the top-rated runner in the field and has run over today's trip, giving him an obvious platform, but he arrives 328 days since his last start and has been winless in his last five outings, which is the concern.

runners_data.name: Cotai Starlight
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here with strong recent form including a win 13 days ago, and she gets a dream scenario if unopposed at the head of affairs; note the STYLE_FIT flag means her P tag reflects a slightly out-of-role deployment but as the actual pace-setter she is in her natural position today.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out with a second, though she was only fifth two starts back, and Cotai Starlight has run over today's trip before; 135 lb from stall nine is no light burden, and our rating of 58 suggests she sits mid-division on merit.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 5f trip on Good ground and has placed on similar going; at eight years old he retains his ability in sharp sprints and a prominent-edge position suits him well off top weight territory handled by Jake Dickson (5lb claim).
runners_data.comment: Albegone arrives on the back of a win last time out, snapping a lean run, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — drawing stall one at 134 lb; the main risk is whether that burden blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho runner in consistent form but unable to win his last five, all on Good ground; the soft surface is a step into less familiar territory and his hold-up style in a big-field sprint requires things to go his way late.
runners_data.comment: Bibendum has experience of today's trip and ground but has managed just one win in his last six starts, with a pair of fifth-place finishes in his two most recent outings making it hard to fancy him strongly, despite a quick 13-day turnaround suggesting he is fit and ready.

runners_data.name: Go Victor
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win over 6f on Good and some soft-ground exposure, though the form figures on softer surfaces are moderate; a hold-up horse who will need gaps to appear in a compressed finish and Billy Garritty must find room late.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Go Victor brings recent winning form and distance-and-going experience to the table, though a nine-run dip three starts back and a ranking of ninth in a field of thirteen suggest he faces a stern test from stall six carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Midnight Lir
runners_data.note: Michael Dods runner who is a genuine hold-up type but is mapped to midfield given the volume of closers in this field — his visor headgear suggests he can be keen early and his soft-going form (sim-going 2/15) shows limited return; the style compromise reduces his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Lir has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 65 ranks him third in a field of thirteen, suggesting he is well treated; however, he is winless in his last six starts, with that eighth last time out the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Solid Bond
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll-trained gelding returning after 83 days off, with a tongue-tie and useful placed effort on soft ground in his history; his prominent style is well-suited to today's race shape and his soft-surface entries are encouraging, though the layoff demands respect.
runners_data.comment: Solid Bond has run over today's distance and going, and her third last time out reads well in this field; winless in recent starts, but 83 days between runs is a minor question mark, and a low draw from stall two could play a part as she carries 131 lb off a mark of 55.

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: A genuine come-from-behind horse — he won over this trip on Good but is being mapped closer than he would naturally race due to field composition; tongue-tie and pad headgear noted, and Tom Eaves will need everything to fall right if this natural closer is unable to find his preferred rearward berth.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Opal Storm has managed just one win in her last six starts, with four finishes of eighth or worse in that sequence, and 131 lb to carry does her no favours; she has run over today's distance and going, and 16 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Never Dark
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a placed effort on Soft going in his history and four wins from 31 runners for Iain Jardine in the past 14 days suggests a yard in form; however, his natural hold-up style is compromised by the crowded rear and his mapping to midfield is a genuine tactical disadvantage over just 5f.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a runner-up three starts back, Never Dark arrives on a quick 13-day turnaround yet to win in his last six starts; experience over today's trip and going helps, but a mark of 54 and 130 lb to carry are the hurdles he must clear.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Terms
runners_data.note: Jardine's second string, a three-year-old who placed on Soft at 6f — the softer ground could suit better than it does older rivals; however, apprentice jockey Cara Tuke (7lb) faces a tough task in a 13-runner sprint where finding the right position out of a natural hold-up role will be the key challenge.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Pivotal Terms nonetheless showed a shade of ability when fourth two runs back, and has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 128 lb from stall 11, she rates a mid-division prospect at best.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith gelding whose sole win came over 5f on Good and who has struggled to replicate it; his natural position at the rear is further compromised by the glut of closers in this race, and his soft-going record (0W0P in similar conditions) adds little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Royal Duke won last time out but that single success from a dire recent record — sixth, fifth, unplaced and seventh in the four starts before it — offers little confidence, and ranked last of the field on our figures, he is hard to fancy at the weights from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies-trained seven-year-old with the best soft-going record in this field (1W2P in similar conditions from 15 runs) and Cieren Fallon takes the ride; his prominent style is naturally suited to the race shape and he is one of the few horses here whose ground credentials are demonstrably proven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a string of mid-pack and out-of-the-frame finishes, Kyber Crystal is hard to fancy from stall 13 carrying 123 lb, and ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a rebound 13 days after her latest run.

runners_data.name: Bust A Moon
runners_data.note: Returns just six days after his last run — a bold move by Derek Shaw — and a natural hold-up horse whose placed effort on Soft at 5f shows some soft-ground aptitude; the very quick turnaround and the forced midfield mapping rather than his preferred rear position are two factors that limit optimism.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 11 of 13 on our figures, Bust A Moon faces a stiff task here; third three starts back offers a sliver of encouragement, and he has run over today's distance and going before, but the overall profile makes him hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Cotai Starlight is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 5f handicap on Good to Soft ground at Carlisle, and with no genuine challenger for the lead likely to push hard early, she can dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than be dragged into a burning pace. That scenario — a single horse in front, travelling well within herself — means the pace will be honest but not fierce, with the tempo shaped by Cotai Starlight's own cruising speed rather than any external pressure. On Good to Soft ground over this minimum trip, a controlled lead in a big field historically compresses the finish, leaving prominent racers in the best position to challenge without having spent themselves early, while true hold-up horses face the added risk of traffic and being forced wider late. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically find their natural rearward berth; Midnight Lir, Opal Storm, Never Dark, Pivotal Terms, Royal Duke, and Bust A Moon are all genuine come-from-behind horses who will inevitably be pushed closer to midfield than they would choose, meaning prominent and stalking profiles — those sitting just off the leader in the first two to four lengths — are best placed in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cotai Starlight Controls, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Starlight gets a clean break and sets a measured, uncontested lead at a pace she dictates.
scenarios.body: Cotai Starlight leads at a sustainable clip and those sitting within two to three lengths in prominent positions are ideally poised to challenge approaching the final furlong, with the soft ground ensuring no late surge from far back. Prominent types like Solid Bond and Kyber Crystal benefit most, travelling economically before picking up the challenge once the leader tires in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Grinds Out Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the Good to Soft surface rides slower and more testing than expected, turning the race into a thorough test of stamina over 5f.
scenarios.body: The pace remains controlled but the ground extracts more from every runner early, meaning horses with proven soft-ground form and solid recent fitness hold a marked edge over those returning from long breaks. Horses with soft-going entries in their history — Never Dark (soft form, recent 13-day return) and Bust A Moon (soft-going placed effort) — would find their true hold-up style rewarded as tiring rivals come back to them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Starlight goes off at an unexpectedly fierce tempo and the pace-setters tie themselves up, opening a late lane for hold-up types.
scenarios.body: With soft ground amplifying the damage of a hot early pace, the field could string out and allow horses tracking from further back to finish fastest; however, many of the nominal hold-up horses here are redistributed from that position and will not be as far back as their natural style demands. The scenario is discounted because the closers most likely to profit — Midnight Lir, Opal Storm — are not truly positioned at the rear and face longer odds of generating the required late momentum.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At The Break
scenarios.trigger: If there is a ragged start or significant interference in the early stages that scrambles positions and disrupts Cotai Starlight's lead.
scenarios.body: A messy break in a 13-runner sprint on a soft surface can leave any horse stuck wide or short of room, turning the race into an unpredictable scrum where form and style matter less than luck. The big field and forced midfield clustering of natural hold-up types increases the risk of traffic incidents late, giving any horse that escapes cleanly on the outer or inner rail an unearned advantage.

watchPoints.text: Cotai Starlight's ability to break cleanly and hold the lead unchallenged is the single most important factor shaping the entire race — if she misses the break or is immediately challenged, the race dynamic changes entirely.

With seven horses mapped to midfield that are natural hold-up types, the final furlong will be congested and any horse drawn wide or trapped on the rail could lose several places in traffic — watch Midnight Lir, Opal Storm and Royal Duke for positioning.

Solid Bond returns from an 83-day break and if he is ring-rusty in the early stages, his prominent style could see him caught flat-footed and unable to maintain his position off the pace — fitness is unproven.

Kyber Crystal's soft-going record (1W2P from 15 runs in similar conditions) stands out in a field where most runners have limited evidence on this type of ground — his credentials are worth monitoring as conditions confirm during the card.

The going for the 3:47 is officially listed as Good to Soft rather than Soft, and any further watering or deterioration through the card would disproportionately favour hold-up types with proven soft form — Never Dark and Bust A Moon would be the primary beneficiaries.

races.name: Quickstep Supporting Andersons Autumn Flooring Offers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Velvet Skies
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a visor, five-year-old who has finished second on similar going at Southwell; eight days since last run is fine but soft Carlisle turf and a front-runner-dominated shape means she needs pace to chase down.
runners_data.comment: Velvet Skies has run over today's trip and going, and our rating edges him ahead of his official mark, making him a sneaky threat from stall 11, though he arrives winless in his last six starts and that inconsistency — including an eighth last time out — is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Donald
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez takes the ride on this hold-up four-year-old who is most at home on good ground; has one placed effort from nine runs on similar going and needs a genuine test that this pace map may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and in good recent nick, Donald arrives here on the back of a fine run 20 days ago, carrying 134 lb from stall 3 over a trip and going he has encountered before; winless in his last six, but his overall profile makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Bay Breeze
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, Tim Easterby's seven-year-old has won and placed at this trip and goes in a hood; form on soft is modest but an uncontested lead changes the equation significantly and Fentiman is an able front-runner pilot.
runners_data.comment: Bay Breeze shaped with promise when fourth two starts back and third four starts back, and our rating of 64 ranks him second among the eleven runners here; he has run over today's trip and going, while the main risk is a winless recent sequence that offers no win to build on.

runners_data.name: Run This Way
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's eight-year-old arrives on a career-best vein of form — two consecutive wins on good ground — with a hood and blinkers and David Nolan aboard; prefers good but will press Bay Breeze and is the most dangerous rival to the leader given its natural position.
runners_data.comment: Run This Way arrives in fine fettle just 14 days since her last start, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and our rating has her narrowly top of this field; the concern is that she has finished third in each of her last two starts rather than converting.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old with a visor has prominent-racing credentials and apprentice Jake Dickson claims five pounds; best form on good ground and soft may blunt her, but she can track the pace and is not without a chance if the leader weakens.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts, Fan Mail has experience over today's trip and going, but that ninth last time out is hard to ignore; 34 days on the sidelines and 132 lb from stall seven give connections plenty to ponder with a gelding seemingly short of his best.

runners_data.name: Zous Juice
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty partners this hold-up five-year-old who has placed twice over seven furlongs on soft and good-to-soft but drops to six; the step down in trip is a question mark and its best recent efforts have come at longer distances.
runners_data.comment: Zous Juice ran second last time out, a promising effort for a gelding yet to win in his last five starts, though a ninth three starts back shows inconsistency; experience over today's trip and going, plus a 60 rating, offer some encouragement from stall 10 carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Little Beck Annie
runners_data.note: Peter Niven's four-year-old has a hood and won last time at Southwell on standard, but her natural inclination is to race from behind — in a field this dominated by hold-up types, she's likely to end up further forward than ideal, which may not suit her finishing pattern.
runners_data.comment: Little Beck Annie brings distance and going experience to the table and her win three starts back shows she can find the front end, but back-to-back fifths in recent starts are a concern, and six days between runs is a sharp turnaround at 125 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Wee Dresser
runners_data.note: Katie Scott's three-year-old has been off 58 days and her form string shows nothing better than third; she instinctively wants to come from behind, but the crowded midfield means she will likely race in a position that isn't natural for her, adding a layer of risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Wee Dresser has done little to inspire confidence, with a run of sixth, seventh and eighth-place finishes dominating her recent record; she has run over today's trip before and returns after 58 days off, but those are slim positives.

runners_data.name: Dream Forever
runners_data.note: Jedd O'Keeffe's three-year-old won on soft at Southwell six days ago and carries blinkers; her true style is rear-end but with so many hold-up types in the same boat she could find herself in an unaccustomed spot, though recent form commands respect.
runners_data.comment: Three unplaced efforts in his last six starts make Dream Forever hard to fancy, and our figures rank him well adrift of the field; he does hold distance and going experience and stall one is a neutral factor, but the overall profile offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's four-year-old carries a hood and has been placed in this grade before; she wants to be ridden from off the pace but the race shape pushes her into midfield, and her soft-ground record at six furlongs doesn't inspire.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Summerstorms Dream faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick turnaround just seven days after a third two starts back suggests some residual form.

runners_data.name: Runninman
runners_data.note: Donald Whillans' three-year-old in a tongue-piece has never threatened in recent runs, posting a 5-6-12-4-7 sequence; he naturally wants to sit last and come late, and with nowhere to race comfortably in that position today, his chances look very slim.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Runninman does at least bring distance and going experience to the table from stall six carrying 119 lb, though a rating of 45 and a midfield ranking among these rivals suggests he faces a stiff task turning things around.

races.paceDynamic: Bay Breeze is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead among the other ten, Duran Fentiman can dictate from the front at a measured, controlled tempo on this Good to Soft Carlisle turf. Run This Way is the only other horse with a natural desire to press forward, giving Bay Breeze a lone accomplice rather than a serious threat, and that combination should produce a sustainable gallop rather than a contested burn-out. The field contains a glut of hold-up horses — Little Beck Annie, Wee Dresser, Dream Forever, Summerstorms Dream, and Runninman are all true hold-up types redistributed into the midfield map positions because there simply is no room at the rear for all of them, meaning they are likely racing out of their natural role. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can genuinely sit off the pace and produce a late burst, but with so many shuffled forward, the clearest beneficiary is the horse that can travel prominently behind the controlled pace, as the moderate tempo on soft ground rewards those racing in the first three or four.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bay Breeze Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Breeze leads uncontested at a comfortable clip and the soft ground blunts the finishing kick of closers.
scenarios.body: Fentiman dictates every yard at a gallop that suits his mount, with soft going rewarding the front-runner's stamina reserves over the final furlong; Run This Way tracks closely but the modest tempo means Bay Breeze never gives up the lead willingly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is comfortable enough for a prominent-racing type to track Bay Breeze and outsprint her in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Run This Way or Fan Mail, both comfortable racing in the first three, get a perfect tow into the race and have enough in the tank to pick off a front-runner who has done too much work; soft ground does not punish their style as harshly as a true hold-up horse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the middle stages to string out the field and create a genuine gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Donald or Velvet Skies, the two hold-up runners with cleaner credentials for this role and acceptable soft-ground form, get a clear passage and finish fastest of all; the scenario is undermined by the likelihood that pace is modest and closers face a wall of rivals who also tried to come from off it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Overcrowded Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed hold-up types jostle for position in midfield, causing interference and an uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: The congestion of five natural hold-up horses all forced forward creates a messy race where no single profile dominates and a horse drawn wide enough to avoid the trouble benefits most; Summerstorms Dream or Dream Forever could emerge from the chaos but this shape remains the least likely given the clear front-runner setting the terms.

watchPoints.text: Bay Breeze is the only true front-runner and if Fentiman gets a clean break from the stalls and bowls along unchallenged, she is controlling the race and the winning post matters.

Run This Way's recent back-to-back wins on good ground may not fully translate to soft, but watch whether David Nolan sends him up to press Bay Breeze early — if he does, he becomes the key pace rival.

Little Beck Annie, Wee Dresser, Dream Forever, Summerstorms Dream, and Runninman are all natural hold-up horses crammed into midfield; monitor the first furlong for traffic and crowding, as their inability to find their natural position could cause interference.

Dream Forever won six days ago on similar soft ground and has the freshest winning form in the field — despite the style-fit concern, keep an eye on whether Jack Nicholls can engineer a clear run from the revised position.

The going report confirms Good to Soft across all distances at Carlisle today; no horse should face a going surprise, but any runner with a soft-ground concern flagged in their history should be treated with caution regardless of how their price drifts.

races.name: Caple - Built Into Every Great Kitchen Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Easterby who ran well here over C&D last time (3rd, soft); came back just 3 days ago suggesting connections are happy, but sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 5 is a concern — reliant on a pace collapse he may not get.
runners_data.comment: Barley has been consistently competitive in recent starts, finishing second and third twice in his last six, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the chief concern is that he returns just three days after his last outing and is yet to win in this recent spell.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a recent C&D win on soft (1st, 8f) and a second course win in his last five; Tudhope's booking is a significant positive upgrade, and his going profile makes him the most compelling horse in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Hostility brings a lively recent profile with two wins in his last six starts, most recently a third last time out after winning two starts back, and he returns after a 21-day break looking fresh; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 133 lb from stall seven is the manageable context here.

runners_data.name: Spiritoftheblues
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who races prominently and has been placed at this trip on good ground repeatedly; no soft-ground run on record is a query, but O'Meara's 4/47 T14 strike rate shows the yard is in reasonable nick and the style is spot-on for the scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Spiritoftheblues has shown consistent placing ability with a second two starts back and a third three starts back, and she has run over today's trip before; 31 days between runs and a pound-for-pound burden of 132 lb from stall five are the checks against her.

runners_data.name: Albemagic
runners_data.note: One of the two confirmed pace-setters; placed twice at this trip on good ground but the soft ground concern is real with only one soft run (7th at 7f); Clifford Lee takes the ride and will need to judge whether to press or concede the lead to Swift Salian early.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Albemagic has posted back-to-back runner-up finishes though our figures rank him well adrift of his rivals here, and 45 days off the track adds a fitness query despite experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Rewired
runners_data.note: Dramatic fitness question after a 472-day absence and all five recent runs were at extreme distances (16-17f); completely out of his normal trip and presumably here for a pipe-opener — hard to factor seriously at 8f.
runners_data.comment: Rewired shaped with plenty of promise when runner-up last time out, and has run over today's trip and going, with a win in his last five starts boosting his claims; the significant concern is a 472-day absence, which leaves his current fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Swift Salian
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner; has been placed four times from five recent outings at this trip on soft or good-to-soft, showing remarkable consistency, though the eight-length defeat last time on soft is a flag; will set the pace and likely be vulnerable late.
runners_data.comment: Swift Salian has been a model of consistency, finishing second three times in his last five starts, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives on an 11-day turnaround with conditions posing no concerns; the main worry is that he remains winless and his last two efforts were an unplaced run and an eighth.

runners_data.name: Arkenstaar
runners_data.note: 110-day break but has won twice on soft at this course and distance — the profile fits if fit; Connor Beasley knows the horse and the track, and a midfield-to-prominent run from this horse would be entirely in keeping with his best form.
runners_data.comment: Arkenstaar has run over today's trip and going before, but his latest run was an unplaced effort and he returns after 110 days off; the two wins in his last five starts show ability, yet that recent blank and the layoff leave questions to answer from stall one carrying 136 lb.

runners_data.name: Zermatt Star
runners_data.note: Won on soft at 8f and that form reads well for the going; however, this horse is a genuine hold-up type forced into a midfield role by the competitive rear-division — racing out of role tempers its prospects despite solid similar-going figures (4/7 placed runs).
runners_data.comment: Zermatt Star won last time out and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround, which underlines her fitness, and she has run over today's trip before; however, three unplaced efforts in her last five starts suggest inconsistency, and 131 lb is a stiff enough burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Recent winner on soft at this trip and course is the obvious selling point; a natural hold-up horse that will find itself pushed into midfield given how many rear-division types are in the field, so the STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful — don't over-rate based on form alone.
runners_data.comment: Tee Aitch Aye arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but ranked ninth of eleven on our figures he faces a stiff task, and 130 lb is a significant burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Bellasio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won at 9f on good ground recently; soft ground record is patchy (10th last time on soft) and the drop back to 8f after a 9f win is fine, but Grant Tuer's T14 rate of 1/8 and the going query make this a watch-and-see runner rather than a leader of the scenario.
runners_data.comment: Bellasio has been unplaced in each of his last two starts and ranks tenth of eleven on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and experience over today's distance and going; the low draw and quick turnaround offer little compensation.

runners_data.name: Epidavros
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature, placed three times at this trip but never on genuinely soft ground — the redistribution into midfield compounds an already uncertain going profile; best watched rather than backed in a race where its natural style is structurally compromised.
runners_data.comment: Epidavros has run over today's trip and going before, but she arrives off an eighth last time out and is winless in her last six starts, making improvement hard to fancy despite a our rating of 71 that nudges above her official mark.

races.paceDynamic: Swift Salian and Albemagic are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the off, likely establishing a genuine pace on this Good To Soft ground over one mile at Carlisle — neither is a natural settler, so the gallop should be honest rather than false. That contested lead creates a race run at a fair clip throughout, which on soft-ish ground over a mile tends to drain stamina reserves and expose those who are not truly getting home. Zermatt Star, Epidavros, and Tee Aitch Aye are genuine hold-up horses but the field holds more rear-division types than the map can accommodate, meaning all three are likely to race further forward than ideal, compressing the midfield and reducing the chance of a true late swooper emerging from the back. This race shape favours prominent racers who can track the pace without over-committing, sit in behind the duel, and pick up the pieces as the front pair tire in the straight — Hostility and Spiritoftheblues fit that profile most naturally.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Swift Salian and Albemagic set a genuine but sustainable gallop and the prominent chasers track them efficiently to the home turn.
scenarios.body: The contested pace softens the front pair late, leaving Hostility and Spiritoftheblues ideally placed to pounce in the final two furlongs on ground they both handle; Hostility's recent course-and-distance win and Tudhope in the saddle make this profile compelling.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Grind Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the leaders establish a decisive break, with no prominent challenger quite bridging the gap.
scenarios.body: Swift Salian's tenacious front-running profile — placed five times this year at this trip — could see it grind out a win if Albemagic fades and nothing can close; soft ground suits a horse that keeps finding off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hot enough to open up a gap along the rail and one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to thread through in time.
scenarios.body: Arkenstaar has winning form on soft and at this course and distance and carries his weight of form; if he gets a clean passage from midfield he has the class to finish off, though the compressed field makes that opening harder to find.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners go off too fast and capitulate sharply, leaving the late runners with a rare opening despite their compromised positions.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Zermatt Star, Epidavros, or Tee Aitch Aye racing as true hold-up horses — all three are redistributed and likely to be further forward than ideal, making a genuine late swoop structurally unlikely; Barley, a hold-up type in good hands, is the best hope if the pace does blow up.

watchPoints.text: Hostility and Swift Salian — watch the early stalls break to see whether Hostility elects to press for the prominent spot or drops in, as that decision will define whether he's ideally placed or caught wide throughout.

Albemagic's soft-ground stamina — if this three-year-old cries enough turning for home after contesting the lead, it will collapse the front two quickly and open the race up for the chasers; the key inflection point is the home turn.

Rewired — 472 days off and a step down from 16f to 8f makes this horse a potential traffic hazard in midfield; Rowan Scott may need to manage him carefully to avoid interference in a compressed field.

Zermatt Star, Tee Aitch Aye, and Epidavros are all genuine hold-up types crowded into the midfield on the map — watch whether any of them visibly anchor themselves at the rear from the start, because if they do their chance evaporates entirely in this pace shape.

Ground creep — the going is officially Good To Soft for the 4:47 race but Carlisle's going reports have been consistent all afternoon; no evidence of deterioration, but runners drawn wide may find softer ground towards the outside of the track.

races.name: Logic's 40th Anniversary Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: One Night Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has placed in similar soft ground (5th/8f/Soft recently), handled Carlisle's test before, and Sam James provides a competent pilot — needs the pace to genuinely soften up rivals before producing a late run, which is plausible here given the two front-runners.
runners_data.comment: One Night Thunder arrives fresh on 11 days' rest, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 82 marks him out as a leading contender from stall 5 carrying 136 lb; the concern is that he is winless in his last six starts, with just one placed effort in that run.

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Jack Nicholls claims 3lbs on a horse with three wins in its last five at 7f (two on Good, one on Soft), returning after 65 days but Iain Jardine's yard is in solid nick at 4/31 over 14 days; prominent style suits a race where the pace is honest without being suicidal, and the soft going is proven.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last six starts give The Gay Blade some claims, but ranked last of the runners on our figures and unplaced last time out after 65 days off, he faces a stiff ask at 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Leopards Rock
runners_data.note: Three-year-old confirmed front-runner sent off by Edward Bethell (5/33 in 14 days), who will push for the lead under Connor Beasley — the contest with Runninsonofagun for early supremacy is the central pace question; recent form shows place efforts at 7-8f and will need to be disciplined if not to burn out on Good to Soft.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Leopards Rock faces a stiff ask here; a return after 42 days and experience over today's trip are the modest positives, though a fifth last time out leaves little to cling to.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the mount on this three-year-old trained by David O'Meara, who has placed twice at 8f on Good and won at 7f — no soft-ground experience recorded in recent history is a mild concern, though the step back to 7f and prominent style off an honest pace is not unfavourable in principle.
runners_data.comment: Sandy Craic arrives in fine fettle, placed in three of her last four starts — second two runs back and third last time out — and has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the concern is whether 132 lb from stall one will anchor her late.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Kodi
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR 75 carrying top weight of 140lbs, wears headgear (p), and the Fahey yard is busy (8/61 in 14 days); soft-ground record is limited at this trip, but prominent racing style with proven 7f course experience means it should be in the mix if the weight doesn't anchor it late.
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye with a second two starts back, and a winner five starts back, Monsieur Kodi brings solid recent form to conditions he has tackled before, and 44 days between runs should leave him fresh enough to go close from stall 11 off 140 lb.

runners_data.name: They All Know Me
runners_data.note: Fahey second string alongside Monsieur Kodi, returned after 19 days, won on Soft at 7f (1/7f/SOF) and placed twice in similar conditions — David Nolan's hold-up ride suits the strong early pace set by the two front-runners, and the soft going is demonstrably within comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: They All Know Me arrives on the back of a win four starts back and returns in good order on 19 days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour; the fourth last time out is the concern, though his rating of 85 marks him as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with blinkers (b), ran only 16 days ago, and Tristan Davidson has the yard firing (4/12 in 14 days) — the clash with Leopards Rock for the lead is key; recent form shows wins at 9f and 7f on Good, but soft-going exposure is limited and the pace duel may cost it at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Runninsonofagun won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but a mark of 71 and 136 lb represent a stiff ask, and two wins in his last six starts suggest he blows hot and cold.

runners_data.name: Albeseeingyer
runners_data.note: Has the profile of a natural prominent racer but, with Sandy Craic, Monsieur Kodi, The Gay Blade and Von Trotter also seeking front-of-midfield positions, Clifford Lee is likely to find space tighter than preferred — zero wins in 15 recent runs and a STYLE_FIT penalty temper expectations here regardless of the shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts but Albeseeingyer has shown consistency of late, finishing third in each of her past two outings, and she has experience of today's distance and going; 131 lb and a ranking of eighth of eleven temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Michael & David Easterby who has won at 7f on Good and placed at 6f and 7f repeatedly — all recent form is on Good ground so soft underfoot is an unknown quantity; Billy Garritty rides and the prominent style should see it competitive early, but the going question is real.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and was runner-up last time out, so Von Trotter arrives in decent nick after 22 days off, and he has run over today's trip before; however, that sixth and seventh in earlier starts hint at inconsistency, and 129 lb is no light burden from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Circle Of Trust
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on Soft and placed at 7f on Soft in last five runs (1W3P in 4 soft/good-to-soft runs), wears blinkers (b), and Tom Eaves partnership is an established one for Kevin Ryan — hold-up style is perfectly matched to a strongly-run 7f on this ground and the form figures in similar conditions are the most compelling in the field.
runners_data.comment: Showed a willing streak when winning two starts back, and a runner-up finish three starts back adds to the case, but he has gone unplaced in his most recent outing and our rating of 74 leaves him in mid-division among these rivals; has run over today's trip and going, and 32 days off should mean fitness is fine.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: True hold-up racer who has been remapped to midfield due to the number of hold-up types in this field — ran just 5 days ago and Tim Easterby's yard is prolific (14/81 in 14 days); the blinkers (b) suggest the yard is trying to sharpen it, but all five recent runs are on Good or better with no soft-ground evidence and the very quick return is a fitness question.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Only Dream Big faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a second last time out offers a sliver of encouragement ahead of a quick five-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Leopards Rock and Runninsonofagun are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead from the break, ensuring a genuine, honest gallop over this 7f on Good to Soft ground at Carlisle — a combination that will stretch the field from the outset rather than allowing a tactical dawdle. The contested early pace into softish ground will drain the leaders' reserves through the final two furlongs, setting up the race for horses who can travel comfortably in mid-division before picking up off the bend. Hold-up and prominent closers who handle soft ground will be the primary beneficiaries, as the honest pace creates a true test of stamina and finishing kick rather than a sprint. This field carries more prominent-racing types than the shape can accommodate at the front — Sandy Craic, Monsieur Kodi, and The Gay Blade are all likely to push for prominent positions, meaning Albeseeingyer is most likely to be squeezed out of its natural prominent slot and forced wider and deeper than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Leopards Rock and Runninsonofagun push each other along at a genuine clip, burning off their reserves before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop on Good to Soft ground sets up a strong-run race where horses held up or tracking at mid-division can reel in the fading leaders from the two-pole home; the soft surface amplifies stamina differences and rewards those who travel without burning petrol early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of Leopards Rock or Runninsonofagun breaks clear and the other capitulates early, allowing a single leader to control tempo.
scenarios.body: A sole front-runner on Good to Soft can regulate fractions, denying closers a fast enough early pace to generate momentum; the leader conserves energy through the first half and has enough left to repel challengers at the distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Horses Win
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but even enough that a prominent racer tracking just off the leaders can pounce decisively approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sandy Craic and The Gay Blade, both proven at 7f in similar conditions, are ideally placed to latch onto the leaders' coattails and hit the rising ground with momentum intact; this shape is particularly suited to those with a high win-rate at this trip and going combination.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race or runners bunch, creating a sprint finish from the final furlong that negates the true closers' natural edge.
scenarios.body: This scenario is the least likely given two genuine front-runners in the field and soft ground, both of which conspire to ensure a run-home test rather than a dash; One Night Thunder has the profile but would need an unusually stop-start pace and a clear run to arrive in time.

watchPoints.text: Leopards Rock and Runninsonofagun will clash for the lead from the stalls — if neither gives way, the pace could be punishing enough on Good to Soft ground to leave both vulnerable inside the final furlong and gift the race to closers.

Circle Of Trust's soft-ground form figures (1W3P in four runs on Soft or Good to Soft) stand out as the strongest course-condition profile in the field — watch whether Tom Eaves can secure a clean passage from mid-division to deliver its late effort.

The Gay Blade returns after 65 days off but Jack Nicholls claiming 3lbs on a horse with three wins from five at 7f is a meaningful booking — a first-time-back fitness concern should be weighed against the form advantage the claim provides.

Only Dream Big ran just five days ago — watch for any signs of fatigue in the closing stages, particularly as it holds no proven form on soft ground and has been repositioned further forward than its natural running style dictates.

Monsieur Kodi carries 140lbs (top weight) as highest-rated runner — if the honest pace on soft ground turns this into a stamina test, monitor whether that weight burden becomes a decisive factor in the final furlong.
